title: Heat and Cold — What They Really Do and When to Avoid Them

hook.en: Hot packs and ice are the most used treatments in clinics and homes, yet many people use them wrongly. Learn what each really does, what the evidence says and the safety rules that protect the skin.
hook.ur: Garam packs aur barf clinics aur gharon mein sab se zyada istemal hone wale ilaj hain, phir bhi bohat se log inhein ghalat istemal karte hain. Seekhein har ek asal mein kya karta hai, evidence kya kehta hai aur jild ki hifazat ke safety usool.

goal.en: By the end, you'll choose heat or cold for a given problem, apply each safely with time limits and skin checks, explain the PEACE and LOVE approach to soft-tissue injury and know when to avoid both.
goal.ur: End tak aap kisi masle ke liye garmi ya sardi chunenge, har ek ko waqt ki hadd aur jild ki jaanch ke saath mehfooz tareeqe se lagayenge, soft-tissue chot ke liye PEACE aur LOVE approach samjhayenge aur jaanenge ke dono se kab bachna hai.

text.en: **Heat** widens blood vessels, relaxes muscle and eases pain, so it suits **stiff, sore, non-swollen** tissue, such as a tight back or neck. **Cold** numbs the area and slows nerve signals, so it can give **short-term pain relief**. Both are **adjuncts**: they help a person to move, but they do not heal the tissue. Neither should be used on skin that cannot feel properly.
text.ur: **Garmi** khoon ki naliyon ko kholti hai, muscle dheela karti hai aur dard kam karti hai, is liye **akhre hue, dardnak, bina sujan** tissue ke liye munasib hai, maslan tight peeth ya gardan. **Sardi** hissay ko sunn karti hai aur nerve ke ishare dheemay karti hai, is liye **thori muddat ka dard mein aaram** de sakti hai. Dono **madadgar** hain: yeh shakhs ko harkat mein madad dete hain, magar tissue ko theek nahi karte. Kisi bhi aisi jild par istemal na karein jo theek se mehsoos nahi karti.

text.en: Think of heat as **warming a stiff rubber band** so it stretches more easily, and cold as **turning down a loud radio**: it quiets the pain signal but does not fix the fault in the radio. Both help you do the real work, which is movement and strengthening.
text.ur: Garmi ko **akhre hue rabar band ko garam karna** samjhein taake woh aasani se khichay, aur sardi ko **bohat tez radio ki awaaz kam karna**: yeh dard ka signal dheema karti hai magar radio ki kharabi theek nahi karti. Dono asal kaam, yani harkat aur strengthening, mein madad dete hain.

title.ur: Garmi ya sardi mehfooz tareeqe se lagana

steps.title: Choose by the problem
steps.detail: Use heat for stiffness and muscle tension without swelling; consider cold for short-term pain relief or after a flare. Ask about previous reactions and medicines. || Masle ke mutabiq chunein

steps.title: Check the skin and sensation
steps.detail: Look at the skin and test light touch and the ability to tell hot from cold. Do not use heat or cold where sensation or circulation is poor. || Jild aur hiss check karein

steps.title: Apply with a barrier
steps.detail: Wrap the pack in a damp towel. Use about 15 to 20 minutes for heat, and 10 to 15 minutes for cold, checking the skin after the first few minutes. Never fall asleep on a heat pack. || Parde ke saath lagayein

steps.title: Pair it with movement
steps.detail: Use heat or cold to make it easier to move, then stretch, strengthen or walk. Review the benefit; if there is none, stop and rethink the cause. || Harkat ke saath jorein

text.en: **Barrier, timer, check.** Always put a layer between the pack and the skin, set a timer and look at the skin. Stop at once for burning, blistering or numbness.
text.ur: **Parda, timer, jaanch.** Pack aur jild ke beech hamesha parda rakhein, timer lagayein aur jild dekhein. Jalan, chhalle ya sunn hone par foran rok dein.

text.en: **Applying heat to a fresh injury.** In the first days after a sprain, heat can increase swelling and bleeding. Use a gentle approach (rest from damaging load, compression, elevation and light movement) and keep heat for stiffness later.
text.ur: **Taaza chot par garmi lagana.** Moch ke pehle dino mein garmi sujan aur bleeding barha sakti hai. Narm approach (nuqsan deh load se aaram, compression, oonchai aur halki harkat) istemal karein aur garmi baad ke akhrapan ke liye rakhein.

question.ur: PEACE aur LOVE approach shuruati soft-tissue chot ke liye kya kehti hai?

text.en: Protect, elevate, avoid anti-inflammatories, compress and educate; then load, stay optimistic, build blood flow with exercise and restore movement

text.en: **Treat the cause as well.** A hot pack is a comfort measure. Teach the patient simple exercises, posture changes or activity pacing so they do not rely on it. For people with diabetes, nerve problems or poor circulation, say plainly that heat and cold can burn without being felt.
text.ur: **Wajah ka bhi ilaj karein.** Garam pack aaram ka zariya hai. Mareez ko saadi exercises, posture mein tabdeeli ya activity pacing sikhayein taake woh isi par mukhtasir na rahein. Diabetes, nerve ke masle ya kamzor circulation wale logon ko saaf batayein ke garmi aur sardi baghair mehsoos kiye jala sakti hain.

question.en: Why is ice not as routine as it used to be for acute injuries?
question.ur: Haali chot par barf pehle ki tarah routine kyun nahi rahi?

answer.en: Good-quality evidence that icing speeds healing or lowers swelling is limited, and it may reduce the early inflammatory signals that start repair. It can still give short-term pain relief, so it can be used for comfort, but the main care is protection, then early, graded loading.
answer.ur: Barf shifa tez karne ya sujan kam karne ka achhi maiyar ka evidence mehdood hai, aur yeh un shuruati sozish ke ishaaron ko kam kar sakti hai jo marammat shuru karte hain. Phir bhi yeh thori muddat ka dard mein aaram de sakti hai, is liye aaram ke liye istemal ho sakti hai, magar mukhya care hifazat, phir jaldi, darje war loading hai.

beats.patient: A 40-year-old office worker has a tight lower back after a day of gardening. There is no swelling, fever or leg symptoms, and his skin sensation is normal. He asks whether to use heat or ice.
beats.assessment: The picture fits a mechanical muscle ache, for which heat is an accepted option for comfort; he has no red flags.
beats.treatment: Advise a warm pack for 15 to 20 minutes with a towel, followed by gentle walking and stretching, and explain that staying active helps most.
beats.reassess: He feels looser, keeps walking and returns to normal activity within a week.

text.en: **Do not apply heat or cold** over broken, infected or numb skin, areas of poor circulation (diabetes, vascular disease), cancer areas, new bleeding or acute swelling, or in people who cannot report discomfort. **Refer** if pain is severe, at night or constant, or comes with fever, weight loss, new weakness or numbness, or a hot swollen calf. Stop at once for burning, blistering or colour change.
text.ur: **Garmi ya sardi na lagayein** toote, infected ya sunn jild, kamzor circulation wali jagahon (diabetes, vascular bimari), cancer ke hissay, naye bleeding ya haali sujan par, ya un logon mein jo takleef bata nahi sakte. **Refer karein** agar dard shadeed, raat ko ya musalsal ho, ya bukhar, wazan ka girna, nayi kamzori ya sunn hona, ya garam soojhi hui pindli ke saath ho. Jalan, chhalle ya rang badalne par foran rok dein.

summary.en: Heat suits stiff, non-swollen tissue and cold gives short-term pain relief; both are adjuncts that help movement, not cures.
summary.ur: Garmi akhre, bina sujan tissue ke liye munasib hai aur sardi thori muddat ka aaram deti hai; dono madadgar hain jo harkat mein madad dete hain, ilaj nahi.

summary.en: Apply with a barrier for 10 to 20 minutes, check the skin, and avoid both where sensation or circulation is poor.
summary.ur: Parde ke saath 10 se 20 minute lagayein, jild check karein, aur jahan hiss ya circulation kamzor ho dono se bachein.

summary.en: For early soft-tissue injury, use PEACE and LOVE: protect first, then load early and progress.
summary.ur: Shuruati soft-tissue chot ke liye PEACE aur LOVE istemal karein: pehle hifazat, phir jaldi load aur darje war izafa.

back.en: For stiff, tight tissue without swelling or inflammation.
